note: The selected X86-64 input bytes are decoded into an InternalInstruction that determines the later MCInst opcode and operands.
The decoded instruction is translated into an MCInst whose opcode chooses the X86 assembly-writer case and whose operands are later printed.
The X86 Intel printer dispatches the decoded MCInst to the generated printInstruction routine.

The temporary access array is only filled through the first zero terminator from the opcode access table, so later entries of the six-byte local array can remain uninitialized even when later operand printing indexes them.
For each printed non-memory register operand, printOperand creates a stack access array and asks get_op_access to populate it for the decoded opcode.
The operand count selected by the generated printer can index an entry of the local access array that get_op_access did not initialize, producing the MemorySanitizer use of uninitialized value.
